prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Transparent 2.5D natural scene-edge module atlas for the Amber Hive insect-civilization fantasy RPG.
Create ONE genuinely transparent RGBA PNG, a STRICT uniform 4 columns x 2 rows, exactly EIGHT separate isolated edge modules, ideally 3072 x 1536. Each module occupies its own equal square cell with at least 12% transparent padding. No cell lines, labels, numbers, letters, border, opaque backdrop, checkerboard pixels, room ground tile, landscape ground plane or connected panorama. Every module is a complete isolated silhouette. The third and fourth upper-row modules must not touch each other or become one scene.
Style consistent across all eight: bright hand-painted cartoon fantasy, high-angle three-quarter near-isometric camera, 2.5D volume, clean colored ink edges, warm upper-left sunlight, soft violet shading. Honey-cream beeswax, translucent golden amber, fresh green giant leaves, vibrant violet insect-wing accents. Distinct insect civilization, playful organic wax/shell/leaf structures. No grey rock wall, rusty machinery, industrial cables or dark cavern.
Exact row-major order, left to right:
ROW 1:
1. Low beeswax terrace rim: a short gently curved honey-cream low step/rim made of irregular wax honeycomb fragments with a few tiny green leaves and violet pollen bells tucked into seams. Broad and LOW, no high blocking wall, no rectangular floor slab attached. Ends organically taper into leaf-root tips.
2. Amber-root corner: a rounded L-shaped terrace corner formed by glossy translucent amber roots, small cream wax nodes and living green leaves. Curved organic junction, no square masonry block, no room ground patch or pool. Useful at an outer garden corner.
3. Giant-leaf shade canopy: an open lightweight shelter with two slender curling amber-root/chitin legs and one huge folded fresh green leaf as a roof, faint violet veins, a small wing pennant. Transparent opening under canopy; no floor/platform or scene behind it. Distinct complete prop.
4. Leaf-wing entrance arch: one open doorway framed by curved green leaf stalks and honey-wax supports with a translucent violet-wing crest overhead. Slim separate feet, clear transparent opening. No surrounding walls, room floor or door leaf filling the opening.
ROW 2:
5. Open honeycomb hive perimeter wall: a short low broken/open lattice of rounded cream wax honeycomb cells entwined with flowers and leaf vines, with a generous arch-like break at center. Sunlight passes through individual cells, their spaces truly transparent. Organic irregular top and tapered ends, NOT a long tall slab or stretched rectangular texture. One complete short edge module.
6. Outer leaf-root entry ramp: a gently sloped woven giant-leaf/root bridge-ramp, about three broad leaf steps, softly curved wax side nubs and amber roots visible beneath. One standalone ramp for an exterior entrance, no attached rectangular floor patch, no river/water/cliff backdrop.
7. Foreground purple-wing foliage: a compact loose cluster of huge soft green leaves, delicate violet wing-shaped blossoms and small yellow pollen dots, lush curved diagonal silhouette for a bottom-screen corner. No pot, no soil patch, no wall. Keep airy holes transparent and tips separate.
8. Honeycomb hive-house distant module: a whimsical small connected group of TWO airy rounded beeswax hive huts with honeycomb windows, giant-leaf roofs, violet-wing hanging curtains, amber root supports and two slender flower stalks. Keep it as a compact architecture-only cutout for distant outer scenery, no hills, sky, clouds, opaque ground base, people or large landscape backdrop. Window/door openings have transparent interiors.
Constraints: alpha zero in every empty area including arch openings, foliage gaps and cell gutters; do not paint a checkerboard or matte. No cast shadows on an imaginary opaque floor. Ground-footing elements belong to each isolated object only. Exactly eight complete sprites with transparent gutters, naturally layered edges, camera and materials consistent with bright hand-painted insect fantasy. Avoid new enemies, characters, machinery, rectangular water holes, huge walls, attached courtyard tilemaps, repeated identical modules, flat vector art, photorealism or labels.
